resources.string: Return address required
Every envelope needs a full sender name and postal address or it is refused.
Full name and number
Address mail with the prisoner\'s full legal name and inmate number; nicknames are not delivered.
Plain envelopes only
White or manila envelopes with no stickers, tape, drawings, or coloured ink.
No stickers or labels
Address labels, stickers, and stamps other than postage are not allowed on the envelope.
One letter per envelope
Envelopes containing letters for more than one prisoner are returned.
Registered post recommended
Ordinary international post is often lost; send letters by registered or tracked mail.
Plain paper only
White lined or unlined paper; no cardstock, construction paper, or scented paper.
Blue or black ink only
Letters written in pencil, marker, crayon, or coloured ink are rejected.
Typed letters allowed
Typed and printed letters are accepted as long as the pages are unbound.
Handwritten letters only
Typed or printed letters are refused; write by hand.
Postcards only
This facility accepts standard-size postcards only; enclosed letters are returned.
No greeting cards
Cards with layers, glitter, pop-ups, or musical parts are refused; a flat card is accepted.
No perfume or lipstick
Scented, stained, or lipstick-marked paper is treated as contaminated and destroyed.
No glue, tape, or staples
Nothing may be glued, taped, or stapled to the pages.
No maps
Maps, including hand-drawn ones, are treated as escape material and confiscated.
No coded messages
Letters containing ciphers, symbols, or unexplained abbreviations are held for investigation.
No drawings by others
Hand-drawn artwork is accepted only from the sender; drawings by children or others are refused.
No third-party mail
Mail that forwards or relays a message from someone else is refused.
No pictures
Letters must be text only; photographs and printed images are returned.
No polaroids
Instant-film photographs are refused because the backing can hide contraband.
No nude or suggestive photos
Photographs showing nudity, underwear, or sexually suggestive poses are destroyed.
No gang signs in photos
Photographs showing hand signs, gang colours, or gang tattoos are refused.
Nothing enclosed
Nothing may be enclosed with a letter: no stamps, cash, cards, or objects of any kind.
Stamps not accepted
Enclosed postage stamps are confiscated; stamps must be bought at the commissary.
No money orders
Funds cannot be sent by mail; use the facility\'s deposit service.
No newspaper clippings
Cuttings and printed articles are refused; write out or describe the content instead.
Printed internet pages allowed
Printed web pages are accepted if they are plain black-and-white text with no images.
Books from publishers only
Books must ship new from a publisher or approved bookseller, never from an individual.
Paperbacks only
Hardcover books are refused; send paperback editions.
No unknown senders
Only senders on the prisoner\'s approved correspondence list are delivered.
Sender approval form
New correspondents must file the facility\'s approval form before their first letter is delivered.
No mail between prisoners
Correspondence with anyone held in another facility requires prior written approval.
Mail opened and read
All incoming mail except legal mail is opened and read by staff before delivery.
Legal mail marked clearly
Mail from a lawyer must be marked Legal Mail with the firm\'s address or it is opened as ordinary mail.
Scanned, not delivered
Incoming mail is scanned by a vendor and shown on a tablet; the paper original is destroyed.
Scanned mail: no colour
Because mail is scanned in greyscale, colour drawings and photos arrive as black and white.
Digital mail only
Letters must be sent through the facility\'s electronic mail service; postal mail is returned.
Delivery not confirmed
The facility does not confirm delivery; expect delays of four to eight weeks.
Holiday mail limits
In December only, up to two cards per sender are accepted.
